and.idleText: No signal on either inlet. The H-spool rests centred in the bore and port 2 is empty.
and.openText: Both inlets are pressurised, so the pressures balance the H-spool in the middle. Air passes through the bypass ports of both discs and streams through the clearance ducts above and below the central shaft into port 2, which receives the lower of the two inlet pressures ({{bar}}).
and.blockedLeftText: Only the left inlet is pressurised. It pushes the spool to the right, and the left disc face covers the passage to port 2. The signal reaches a dead end and port 2 stays empty.
and.blockedRightText: Only the right inlet is pressurised. It pushes the spool to the left, and the right disc face covers the passage to port 2. The signal reaches a dead end and port 2 stays empty.
and.caption: Stepped H-spool: two sealing discs on a shaft, landing on shoulder seats · clearance ducts around the shaft

regulator.idleText: No pressure at any port. The spring pushes the diaphragm down and holds the poppet open.
regulator.regulatingText: Downstream pressure ({{out}}) is below the set point ({{set}}). The spring keeps the diaphragm down and the poppet open, so supply air ({{in}}) flows from port 1 to port 2.
regulator.holdingText: Port 2 has reached the set point ({{set}}). Pressure under the diaphragm balances the spring, so the diaphragm rises and the poppet throttles or closes the gap: the output stays steady at {{out}}.
regulator.ventingText: Port 2 ({{out}}) is above the set point ({{set}}). The diaphragm lifts off the relief seat in its centre and the excess air escapes through the bonnet vent until the pressure falls back.
regulator.caption: Adjusting knob and spring · sensing diaphragm · throttling poppet and seat
regulator.captionRelieving: Adjusting knob and spring · diaphragm with relief seat · throttling poppet · vent port 3

relief.idleText: No pressure at the inlet. The spring presses the conical poppet onto its seat.
relief.closedText: Inlet pressure ({{in}}) is below the set pressure ({{set}}), so the spring keeps the poppet on its seat and nothing escapes.
relief.openText: Inlet pressure has reached the set pressure ({{set}}). The force on the poppet overcomes the spring preload and lifts it, discharging air to the vent until the pressure falls back.
relief.caption: Adjusting screw and spring · conical poppet · seat

gauge.liveText: Reading {{bar}}. Pressure at the port flexes the Bourdon tube, which turns the needle over the 0–10 bar scale: the deflection is proportional to the measured pressure.
gauge.idleText: The port is at atmospheric pressure, so the needle rests at zero.
gauge.caption: Same dial and needle as the air receiver's gauge

quickExhaust.idleText: There is no pressure at any port. The rubber disc rests against the inlet seat, so port 1 is sealed and the exhaust is open to atmosphere.
quickExhaust.fillText: Supply pressure ({{supply}}) lifts the disc onto the exhaust seat and seals port 3 to atmosphere. The edges of the disc flex, and the air rushes past them straight into working port 2 ({{work}}).
quickExhaust.exhaustText: Port 1 has dropped, so the pressure in the working line ({{work}}) drives the disc down onto the inlet seat. The supply is sealed and the whole exhaust cross-section opens: the cylinder air dumps directly to atmosphere through port 3 instead of travelling back through the control valve.
quickExhaust.caption: Flexible disc between the inlet seat (1) and the exhaust seat (3)

or.idleText: No signal on either inlet. The ball floats in the chamber and port 2 is empty.
or.bothText: Both inlets are pressurised and the ball floats between the seats. Fluid streams around the sphere from both sides, so port 2 carries the higher pressure ({{bar}}).
or.leftText: Pressure on the left inlet drives the ball onto the opposite, right conical seat and seals the idle inlet. The left fluid curves around the sphere and flows out through port 2 without leaking away through the right inlet.
or.rightText: Pressure on the right inlet drives the ball onto the opposite, left conical seat and seals the idle inlet. The right fluid curves around the sphere and flows out through port 2 without leaking away through the left inlet.
or.caption: Floating ball between two conical seats

spool.midFloat: Mid-position — P blocked, A and B open to tank
spool.centring43: Opposed centring springs hold the spool in the middle, so its lands seal P and both tank chambers and the cylinder lines A and B are shut in. {{description}}
spool.centringFloat: Opposed centring springs hold the spool in the middle: one land seals P while A and B stay open to tank, so the cylinder floats. {{description}}
spool.centring: Opposed centring springs hold the spool in the middle, so its three lands sit over Ports 5, 1 and 3 and the cylinder lines are shut in. {{description}}

groove.supplyWork: A groove bridges supply Port 1 to working Port {{ports}}
groove.workExhaust: Working Port {{work}} vents through the groove to exhaust Port {{exhaust}}

spool.supplyBlocked: Supply Port 1 is blocked by a land
spool.workTrapped: Working Port {{port}} is closed — the cylinder line is trapped at {{bar}}
spool.workSealed: Working Port {{port}} is closed — its volume is sealed between two lands

cushion.normalText: The piston is in mid-stroke. The fluid ahead of it leaves freely through the main port, so the piston runs at full speed.
cushion.noneText: This cylinder has no cushioning (set End-Position Cushioning in the properties to add it). The piston runs at full speed into the end cap and stops metal-to-metal, apart from the engine's end-position damping.
cushion.throttledText: The cushion spear has entered the {{end}} end-cap cavity and shut the main exit. The trapped fluid can only escape through the {{needle}}, so pressure builds ahead of the piston and slows it down smoothly before the cap.
cushion.seatedText: The piston has come to rest against the {{end}} end cap with its spear inside the cavity. The main exit is closed; any residual fluid can only seep through the needle valve.
cushion.restText: The piston is stationary between the cushion zones. Both chambers are connected to their main ports.
cushion.leavingText: The piston is driving away from the end cap. The spear is still in its cavity, so the incoming fluid enters through the bypass passage beside the needle valve until the spear clears the cavity mouth.
cushion.spear: Tapered cushion spear on the piston · needle valve in the end cap

single.rest: At rest — spring holds the piston back
single.restText: Port A is unpressurised, so the return spring pushes the piston against the rear cap. The spring side of the piston breathes through the vent hole.
single.extendingText: Air at {{rear}} pushes the piston forward against the return spring, which now balances {{spring}}. The piston keeps going until the spring balances the air at {{percent}} of the stroke{{end}}. The air ahead of the piston escapes through the vent hole.
single.retracting: Retracting — spring drives the piston back
single.retractingText: The spring force ({{spring}} equivalent) now exceeds the air in the rear chamber ({{rear}}), so it pushes the piston back{{until}}. Fresh air is drawn in through the vent hole.
single.untilBalance: until the two balance at {{percent}} of the stroke
single.fullText: The piston is at the end of its stroke with the spring fully compressed ({{spring}} equivalent). The rear chamber holds {{rear}}; if port A is vented the spring returns the piston.
single.held: Held mid-stroke — pressure balances the spring
single.heldText: The piston is stationary at {{percent}} of the stroke: {{rear}} on the piston is balanced by the spring force ({{spring}} equivalent). Raise the pressure to {{full}} or more to reach the end of the stroke.
single.preloadText: Port A holds {{rear}}, which does not yet overcome the spring preload ({{preload}} equivalent), so the piston stays on the rear cap.
single.spring: Return spring between the piston and the front cap · single working port in the rear cap
single.balance: air {{air}} bar · spring {{spring}} bar equivalent · balance at {{balance}}% stroke

flow.idleDesc: Nothing is flowing through the valve. The needle is set to {{opening}} % open.
flow.throttleDesc: The fluid passes from port {{from}} to port {{to}} only through the gap between the needle and its conical seat. The needle is {{opening}} % open, so the flow, and with it the speed of the actuator, is limited to {{opening}} % of the free value. The actuator still completes its full stroke.
flow.meteredDesc: Pressure at port 1 presses the check poppet onto its seat and the sealing ring closes the bypass. The fluid can only take the throttle path, through the gap around the needle, which is {{opening}} % open.
flow.freeDesc: Pressure at port 2 lifts the check poppet off its seat against the light spring. The fluid rushes through the wide bypass passage at full speed, whatever the needle setting.

check.closedDesc: Nothing is pushing the ball forward, so it rests in the conical seat. The valve is closed.
check.openDesc: Pressure at port 1 rolls the ball off the conical seat into the retention cage. The fluid passes around it through the full bore.
check.blockedDesc: Pressure at port 2 drives the ball into the conical seat. The seal is hermetic, so nothing flows back from port 2 to port 1.
check.crackClosedDesc: Port 1 holds {{bar}} bar, below the cracking pressure of {{crack}} bar. The calibrated spring keeps the ball on its seat.
check.crackIdleDesc: The spring, pre-tensioned to {{crack}} bar, holds the ball in its seat. The valve opens only when the pressure at port 1 exceeds {{crack}} bar.
check.crackOpenDesc: Port 1 holds {{bar}} bar, above the cracking pressure of {{crack}} bar. The ball lifts off its seat and compresses the spring inside its guide sleeve; the fluid flows to port 2.

reservoir.emptyText: The vessel is at atmospheric pressure and holds no stored air. When the line upstream is pressurised through a throttle, the vessel starts to fill.
reservoir.chargingText: Air flows in through the inlet. The vessel holds {{bar}} of the {{supply}} line pressure and is rising {{rate}} bar/s. The rate falls in proportion to the remaining difference, so the pressure follows an exponential curve towards the supply; a narrower throttle upstream stretches it.
reservoir.chargedText: The vessel has equalised with the line at {{bar}}. No air flows now; the stored volume is ready to feed the pilot line.
reservoir.dischargingText: The upstream line has dropped and the vessel empties backwards through the inlet, falling {{rate}} bar/s. Through the free-return check valve of a one-way flow control it empties at once; through a plain throttle it empties as slowly as it filled.

timer.idleText: There is no pressure on pilot port 12. The chamber is empty and the return spring holds the spool shut: port 1 is blocked and port 2 is vented through port 3.
timer.delayText: The signal on port 12 is forced past the needle, {{opening}} % open, and fills the accumulation chamber ({{bar}} of the {{threshold}} needed). The pilot force is still below the spring preload, so the spool stays seated: port 1 is blocked and port 2 is vented to port 3.
timer.switchedText: The chamber has reached {{threshold}}, so the pilot force overcame the spring preload and the spool snapped to the right: port 3 is closed and port 1 is joined to port 2, which now feeds the working line.
timer.resettingText: The signal on port 12 is gone. The check valve in the bypass unseats and the chamber empties backwards in milliseconds; the spring returns the spool and port 2 is vented again.
